core_meaning.primary_meaning: Abda represents Arabic عبدة (ʿabdah), a feminine form associated with a female servant or worshipper; “of God” is not literally present in the standalone form.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: The name is the Arabic word itself, used unchanged as a given name rather than a derived or diminutive form.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The Arabic form عبدة is feminine and related to the root ع ب د. The source's phrase “servant of Allah” adds الله, which is not present in the word. The lexical gloss should be distinguished from the religious interpretation sometimes attached to it.

faq.a: Abda represents Arabic عبدة (ʿabdah), a feminine form associated with a female servant or worshipper.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abda?
faq.a: The recorded form عبدة is Arabic and is grammatically feminine.
Yes. The underlying Arabic form recorded here is عبدة (ʿabdah).

faq.q: What is the root of Abda?
faq.a: The form is associated with the Arabic root ع ب د (ʿ-b-d), related to servitude and worship.
Abda is used in some Muslim naming contexts, but the standalone word does not literally include the divine name Allah.
This record does not establish Abda as a Qur'anic personal name; Arabic origin alone is not proof of scriptural status.

faq.q: What does Abda mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, عبدہ is glossed here as بندی، خادمہ، عبادت کرنے والی; “اللہ کی بندی” adds an element not present in the form.
The supplied “ab-da” is an approximate romanization of عبدة (ʿabdah).

faq.q: Is Abda a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies Abda as feminine, consistent with the grammatical form; regional name-frequency data is not supplied.
